oneLiner: The clear No. 2 custom AI silicon and optical interconnect franchise, with accelerating revenue and a potential Google win, priced at a premium that assumes it keeps its sockets.
thesis: AI demand is accelerating, not decelerating. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to a record $2.418B, Q2 was guided to $2.7B (+35% YoY), and management says growth accelerates each quarter of FY27.
Custom XPU pipeline is broadening. Custom silicon is expected to more than double in FY28 on a new tier-1 XPU ramp plus 10+ XPU-attach programs, on top of AWS Trainium and Microsoft Maia work.
Electro-optics is a second growth engine. Interconnect revenue is now expected to grow 70%+ in FY27 (raised from 50%) on 800G/1.6T optics, 51.2T switching, and DCI modules.
Celestial AI adds a scale-up optics option. The $3.25B Photonic Fabric acquisition (closed Feb 2, 2026) targets a ~$500M annual run-rate exiting FY28, ~$1B exiting FY29.
Google optionality. April 2026 reports (The Information) put Marvell in talks on two Google inference chips, with design finalization targeted for 2027 and ~2M units discussed.

latestProse: Q1 FY27 (April-end) revenue was a record $2.418B, +28% YoY and above guidance, with data center at $1.83B (+27% YoY, 76% of revenue) and communications/other at $585.1M (+29%). Non-GAAP gross margin was 58.9%, non-GAAP EPS $0.80; GAAP EPS was only $0.04 on acquisition-related and SBC charges. The disclosure that matters most: management called AI bookings 'exceptional' and significantly raised both FY27 and FY28 revenue expectations, citing 1.6T optics, custom XPU/XPU-attach, and scale-up optical (NPO/CPO) demand.
guidanceProse: Q2 FY27 guide: revenue $2.70B plus or minus 5% (midpoint +35% YoY), non-GAAP gross margin 58.25-59.25%, non-GAAP EPS $0.93. Call commentary lifted FY27 revenue expectations to roughly $11.5B and the FY28 target to about $16.5B, with data center growing ~50% in FY27 and ~55% in FY28 and a longer-term custom silicon target above $10B by FY29 (management targets, not formal guidance). The debate: whether these targets survive disputed analyst claims (SemiAnalysis, Benchmark) that Trainium 3/4 back-end work shifted to Alchip - unconfirmed by Marvell or Amazon.

guide.label: Q2 FY27 revenue guide
guide.sub: Midpoint +35% YoY; non-GAAP EPS $0.93; reports Aug 27, 2026

segments: Data center: $1.83B, 76% of Q1 FY27 revenue, +27% YoY (custom compute, electro-optics, switching, storage)
Communications and other: $585.1M, 24% of revenue, +29% YoY
Within data center, interconnect guided +70%+ in FY27; custom silicon to more than double in FY28
competitive: Broadcom: dominant custom-ASIC rival (~$21B 2026 AI revenue est.; Google TPU deal through 2031); Marvell holds ~20-25% of custom ASIC design share
Alchip/MediaTek: lower-cost back-end design challengers; alleged Trainium 3/4 wins are the key bear claim
Nvidia: merchant-silicon gravity plus NVLink Fusion ecosystem shapes hyperscaler make-vs-buy
Astera Labs/Credo: niche connectivity competitors; Marvell leads PAM4 optical DSPs
Customer set: AWS (Trainium), Microsoft (Maia), Meta, Google (Axion CPU) across 18 reported design wins
moat: Deep multi-generation co-design relationships with hyperscalers, leading PAM4 optical DSP and 224G SerDes IP, and now Celestial's Photonic Fabric plus XConn CXL switching give Marvell a full electrical-plus-optical interconnect stack few can match. Switching costs on in-flight XPU programs are high, though the alleged Trainium loss shows the moat is per-socket, not permanent.
risks: Socket churn. Reported (unconfirmed) loss of AWS Trainium 3/4 back-end work to Alchip triggered a December 2025 downgrade; custom ASIC wins are contestable every generation.
Extreme concentration. Data center is 76% of revenue, dominated by a handful of hyperscalers; one program cancellation moves the model.
Thin GAAP economics. GAAP EPS of $0.04 vs $0.80 non-GAAP shows heavy SBC, amortization, and acquisition costs; Celestial adds ~27M shares plus up to $2.25B earnouts.
Google may not convert. Talks were early-stage with no signed contract; Broadcom and MediaTek are incumbents.
High-beta AI trade. Beta 2.25; the stock fell ~34% from its June peak ($329.88) in the July AI selloff.
Margin mix. Custom silicon carries below-corporate gross margins, capping margin expansion as it scales.
catalysts: Aug 27, 2026: Q2 FY27 results ($2.7B guide) and FY27/FY28 updates
Oct 6, 2026: Investor Day - custom pipeline and Celestial detail expected
Through 2026: Trainium 3 volume ramp and Maia 200 progress; 1.6T optics ramp
pricedIn: At $217.08 (Aug 12; ~$190B market cap), MRVL trades at ~75x trailing and ~48x forward earnings, down ~34% from its June record $329.88 after the July AI-trade pullback. Consensus is Strong Buy with a ~$257 target. The price already embeds the raised ~$11.5B FY27 outlook; the debate is whether the $16.5B FY28 target and $10B+ FY29 custom ambition are credible given contested Trainium sockets - bulls see a cheap call on a Google win, bears see Broadcom-style pricing without Broadcom-style contract visibility.

scenarios.bear: Trainium/Maia share losses are confirmed and Google talks lapse; custom growth stalls in FY28, AI capex digests, and FY28 revenue lands nearer $13B. Forward multiple compresses toward 30x on cut estimates; stock revisits the $120-140 area.
scenarios.base: FY27 delivers ~$11.5B (+~40%) with quarterly acceleration; tier-1 XPU and 1.6T optics ramp on schedule, FY28 approaches the $16.5B target. Stock grinds back toward the $257 consensus target as Aug 27 results and the Oct 6 Investor Day de-risk the roadmap.
scenarios.bull: A signed Google inference program plus retained AWS/Microsoft sockets validate a $10B+ custom business by FY29; Celestial wins scale-up optical sockets. Estimates move materially higher and the stock retests and exceeds the $330 high.

valPresets.note: FCF basis works here (record operating cash flow, modest capex), but note GAAP earnings are a fraction of non-GAAP - SBC is a real cost the DCF ignores.
